newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs bounce back, seen higher.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs bounce back, seen higher.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures bounced back from lows on Friday as players covered positions ahead of the weekend after the release of stronger than expected data spurred sales earlier.
"There was some buying out of London. I think it was just people covering their shorts. There was no news," a trader with a U.S. futures house said.
He said the lead December Euroyen contract shot to a high of 99.11 after breaching a recent stubborn barrier at 99.08. He said the contact's next target was at 99.16.
It was quoted at 99.10 at 1115 GMT after falling to a low of 99.03 against an IMM close at 99.07.
But a trader with a Japanese futures house said the contract's recent gains were caused by people who had sold it short being squeezed and added he would sell around 99.10.
Euroyen futures came under pressure earlier on news Japan's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) rose a real 1.6 percent for the January-March quarter from the previous quarter, or an annualised 6.6 percent.
The market had been expecting January-March GDP to grow by about four to five percent on an annualised basis.
September JGBs ended at 124.01 against a previous 123.61.
"I think the JGBs are underperforming a bit, partly because of the run-up in U.S. treasuries, which give better yields," the trader at the U.S. brokerage said.

Eurodollar futures shed some of their overnight gains but dealers said there were growing hopes the U.S. Federal Reserve would leave rates steady at its July meeting as recent economic data suggested little inflationary pressure.

"People think there's no reason for the Fed to tighten now but I have a feeling they still might, just to go through the motions. So in the medium-term, I'd look for levels to go short (Eurodollars)," the trader said.

December Eurodollars ended at unchanged against their IMM close at 93.930 ahead of the release of the U.S. May Producer Price Index (PPI). The consensus forecast in a Reuters survey sees a 0.1 percent rise in both the PPI and core PPI.
